born.why: The code prioritizes survival by eating when starving or targeted, uses a simple majority vote on past harm to reject poisonous species, and cautiously tastes novel fruits only when well-fed, while carrying safe fruits for later if not currently needed.

The code distinguishes between safe, risky, and unknown fruits by comparing past positive vs negative outcomes for each species, prioritizing eating safe foods when hungry and only tasting or seeking risky/unknown foods under specific hunger constraints to minimize starvation risk while maximizing exploration.

The code improves survival by distinguishing between novel, proven-safe, and proven-poisonous fruits using historical data, prioritizing eating when starved, tasting unknowns at safe hunger levels, and leaving confirmed poisons, while retaining the innate preference fallback.

This code improves survival by implementing a "safety-first" policy with starvation overrides, distinguishing between safe, risky, and novel fruits using recent history, prioritizing eating when hungry and carrying when not starving to build pantry reserves, and avoiding known poisonous species more aggressively.

This code improves survival by prioritizing known-safe fruits for carrying (storage efficiency), eating only when hungry or if no carry option exists, and using 'taste' cautiously for novel fruits to update the diary, while defaulting to 'leave' for known-poisonous species unless starvation forces action.

The code prioritizes survival by eating when starving, learning via tasting for novel fruits unless desperate, avoiding known poisonous species, and carrying safe food when not immediately hungry to build reserves.
